trust_decision.summary: How much memory the zstd decoder may allocate while inflating an HPKE-sealed query string is decided once, in the package-level decoder initialiser in pkg/hpke/url.go:167-169; before the fix that decoder had no decoded-size limit, so a tiny sealed `q` parameter could inflate without bound inside DecryptURLValues.

landing_point.why: The summary names unbounded zstd decompression on the HPKE path; the repo has exactly one zstd reader (pkg/hpke/url.go:167) and exactly one caller of DecodeAll (pkg/hpke/url.go:172), so an engineer who reads the advisory lands directly on the shared decoder and its single consumer.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API hpke.DecryptURLValues (pkg/hpke/url.go:80) -> decodeQueryStringV2 (pkg/hpke/url.go:171); reached from authenticate /.pomerium/sign_in (internal/authenticateflow/stateless.go:175), the authenticate pre-auth IdP lookup used by /.pomerium/ routes (authenticate/handlers.go:476 -> internal/authenticateflow/stateless.go:269, and authenticate/handlers.go:342), and proxy /.pomerium/callback (proxy/handlers.go:105-107 -> internal/authenticateflow/stateless.go:393)
fix_sites.module_kind: public library package (pkg/hpke), shared package-level decoder configured once

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate HPKE v2 payloads must still inflate: the pinned test asserts a 128 KiB query string compresses to under 1024 bytes and must decrypt back (pkg/hpke/url_test.go:69-78), and real payloads carry the whole protojson identity profile plus tokens (internal/urlutil/known.go:72-77). An over-broad fix (cap the base64 `q` length, reject high compression ratios, or cap output at a few KiB) breaks those legitimate frames; the uncompressed V1 path (pkg/hpke/url.go:102-105) must also keep working untouched.

O6_input_shapes: v2 sealed query parameter `q`, raw-URL-base64 without padding (pkg/hpke/hpke.go:248-250), inflated at pkg/hpke/url.go:171-177
attacker-crafted zstd frame whose content size / window exceeds 4 MiB - now rejected by the limit added at fix.diff:13
an in-repo-produced frame from encodeQueryStringV2 with an 8 KiB window (pkg/hpke/url.go:152-157), which must keep decompressing
v1 sealed query parameter `pomerium_hpke_query`, uncompressed (pkg/hpke/url.go:102-105) - the fix does not touch it and has no decompression to bound

O7_producer.where: pkg/hpke/url.go:159-161 (encodeQueryStringV2 zstd-compresses the query string that the peer later must inflate); the mirror decoder is pkg/hpke/url.go:171-177

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A compressed legacy variant: decodeQueryStringV1 gaining its own zstd (or other codec) branch with a freshly created, uncapped reader
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: V1 and V2 already sit side by side as two decode helpers in the same file, and V1 was deliberately kept for compatibility, so a maintainer adding a V1.5/bundle format would copy the V2 helper and likely instantiate its own decoder rather than reuse the capped one.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second size constant / body path for a compressed HPKE payload delivered outside the query string (POST body, cookie, header)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same package already keeps a separate fixed limit (defaultMaxBodySize) for the JWKS read at pkg/hpke/http.go:47, showing the codebase's habit of one constant per transport path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second flow (or a stateless bundle reload) that decrypts and inflates stored callback state with its own decoder instead of calling pkg/hpke
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The package already contains two parallel flows (stateful.go and stateless.go) with duplicated callback/sign-in methods, so a third variant that inlines its own decompression is a realistic copy-paste.

O9_family: decompression bomb / uncontrolled resource consumption (CWE-409, CWE-400, CWE-1284): an attacker-supplied compressed frame is inflated without bounding the decoded size before the sender key is validated (internal/authenticateflow/stateless.go:393-399)

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.25.4 (go.mod:3); plain go build / go test, no cgo, no GPU
O10_build.project_tests: pkg/hpke/url_test.go:12-79 (TestEncryptURLValues: v1, v2, and a 'compresses' case asserting a 128 KiB payload encodes to <1024 bytes; no decompression-limit test at the pinned commit) and pkg/hpke/url_test.go:81-92 (BenchmarkZSTD); internal/urlutil/known_test.go:19-35 and :78-100 (Encrypt/Decrypt round-trip). There is no unit test for internal/authenticateflow/stateless.go (that package has stateful_test.go and authenticateflow_int_test.go only).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Bound the request instead of the decoder: add a length/ratio check on the `q` form value at one caller (internal/authenticateflow/stateless.go:393) or in DecryptURLValues. The compressed payload is tiny, so nothing is actually bounded and the other callers (stateless.go:175, :269, :307) stay unprotected.

out_of_scope_notes: internal/zero/api/download.go:69 calls gzip.NewReader(r) with no decoded-size limit on a downloaded bundle - a different subsystem (zero/API bundle transfer), outside this advisory's HPKE query-string protection; not pursued.
internal/zero/api/api.go:130 is the matching zstd writer for that subsystem; there is no unguarded zstd decode there.
pkg/hpke/http.go:13's defaultMaxBodySize (4 MiB) bounds only the JWKS response read, not any decompression.
unverified: O1 is counted at the flawed site: hpke.DecryptURLValues is the single public entry point into the sink. Three HTTP route families reach it (authenticate /.pomerium/ pre-auth IdP lookup: authenticate/handlers.go:476,342 -> internal/authenticateflow/stateless.go:269; /.pomerium/sign_in -> internal/authenticateflow/stateless.go:175,:307; proxy /.pomerium/callback -> internal/authenticateflow/stateless.go:393), but all share the one package-level decoder, so there is no per-route fix and j_multi_site is 0.
Repo size not measured (shell/du unavailable in this session); pomerium is a large Go monorepo, so tiny_repo is unlikely and giant_repo (>1.5 GB) was not confirmed.
Advisory text was not available locally; the 'pre-auth' wording and the 4 MiB threshold were read from the candidate summary and the diff only.

Whether the residual 4 MiB-per-request allocation that still happens before the sender key is validated (internal/authenticateflow/stateless.go:393-399) remains a practical memory-exhaustion vector under concurrency was not assessed.
Whether 4 MiB is comfortably above the largest legitimate identity profile (internal/urlutil/known.go:72-77) was not measured; if it is not, the published fix itself would be over-broad.
Latest release is 'none', so present_in_latest is unknown; O8 is empty so nothing depends on it.
